## Keywords

## 19.1 From the LAN to the Internet

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- A LAN connects the devices of one place.
- A switch joins the cables, and an access point gives Wi-Fi.
- A router connects the LAN through the ISP to the Internet.
- **Do it:** Draw the network at your home. Which box is the router?
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
![](images/lan-map.png)
:::
::::

## Try it 1 · The devices

a) Which device joins the cables of the office PCs?
b) Which device gives Wi-Fi to the test phones?
c) Which device connects the LAN to the ISP?

::: {.answer}
a) a switch
b) an access point
c) a router
:::

## 19.2 Addresses and the DNS

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- An IP address identifies a device, such as 192.168.1.23.
- Private addresses work only inside the LAN.
- The DNS turns a name into an IP address.
- **Do it:** Find the IP address of your phone. Is it private?
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
![](images/addresses.png)
:::
::::

## Example · The phone finds the server

The game of Rami's phone knows only the name play.example.net.
**How do its packets reach the server?**

::: {.reveal}
1. The phone asks the **DNS**, and the answer is **198.51.100.7**.
2. It sends the packets to its **default gateway**, the router.
3. The routers of the Internet **forward** them to 198.51.100.7.
:::

## Try it 2 · Addresses

a) Is 192.168.1.23 a private or a public address?
b) What does the DNS do with play.example.net?
c) Which device is the default gateway of a laptop?

::: {.answer}
a) private
b) It finds its IP address.
c) the router
:::

## 19.3 Packets and protocols

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- Data travels in packets with two addresses.
- Protocols work in four layers.
- TCP is reliable, and UDP is fast.
- **Do it:** Send packets with TCP and UDP at 20 % loss. What is different?
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
![](images/tcp-udp.png)
:::
::::

## Live demo · Packet Journey

{{< sim file="sims/packet-journey.html" poster="sims/packet-journey.png" title="Packet Journey: TCP or UDP?" task="**Show:** send a purchase with TCP and no loss, then 20 % loss, then the same with UDP. **Ask:** which protocol fits the player positions, and why?" >}}

## Example · Two kinds of data

The online race of Pocket Quest sends positions and purchases.
**Which protocol does each one use?**

::: {.reveal}
1. **Positions** go 30 times per second over **UDP**, because the next one is newer anyway.
2. **A purchase** goes over **HTTPS on TCP**, because every byte must arrive.
3. The **leaderboard** and the save game also use TCP.
:::

## Try it 3 · TCP or UDP

a) Which protocol carries voice chat?
b) Which protocol carries a chat message?
c) What does TCP do with a lost packet?

::: {.answer}
a) UDP
b) TCP
c) It sends it again.
:::

## 19.4 Network quality

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- Latency is the time of a packet there and back.
- Jitter is how much the latency changes.
- Packet loss counts the packets that never arrive.
- **Do it:** Compare the ping near and far from the router. What changes?
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
![](images/net-quality.png)
:::
::::

## Try it 4 · Quality (harder)

a) What is the packet loss when 6 of 8 packets arrive?
b) What is the problem when the ping is 30, 180, 40 and 210 ms?
c) Does 200 Mbit/s with 8 % loss give a smooth race?

::: {.answer}
a) 25 %
b) high jitter
c) No, the lost packets make players jump.
:::

## Summary

- A switch, an access point and a router build a LAN and connect it to the Internet.
- IP addresses find devices, and the DNS turns names into addresses.
- Data travels in packets, and protocols work in four layers.
- Purchases go over TCP, and live positions go over UDP.
- Games need low latency, low jitter and almost no packet loss.
